source.text: וַיַּ֛עַשׂ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֥ח הָעֹלָ֖ה עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים חָמֵשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת אָרְכּ֜וֹ וְחָֽמֵשׁ־אַמּ֤וֹת רָחְבּוֹ֙ רָב֔וּעַ וְשָׁלֹ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת קֹמָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made the altar of the burnt offering [of] woods of acacia; five cubits its length and five cubits its breadth, square, and three cubits its height.

en.L: And he made the altar of burnt offering [of] acacia wood, 5 cubits its length and 5 cubits its breadth, square, and 3 cubits its height.
en.B: He made the altar of burnt offering out of acacia wood. It was square, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} on each side and {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|3 cubits}} high.
en.R: Bezalel made the altar for burnt offerings out of acacia wood. It was square, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} on each side and {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|3 cubits}} tall.

decisions.choice: he made: Bezalel made
decisions.reason: The one who makes the furnishings in chapters 37-38 is Bezalel, named at 37:1 and again in verse 22.

decisions.choice: the altar of burnt offering: made as commanded in 27:1-8
decisions.reason: Verses 1-7 tell how the bronze altar was made, following the instructions of 27:1-8 almost word for word. The notes on those verses explain its parts; the notes here point back to them.

decisions.choice: cubit: a measure of length, from the elbow to the tip of the fingers, about 18 inches
decisions.reason: The cubit was the length of a forearm, about 18 inches (about 45 centimeters). The altar was about 7 1/2 feet square and about 4 1/2 feet high (27:1).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the size of the altar in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative. Literal keeps cubits, written as numerals like every measurement.

decisions.choice: Bezalel
decisions.reason: Readable names Bezalel for "he" (m1), since the chapter opens without naming him. Literal and Balanced keep "he".

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ קַרְנֹתָ֗יו עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פִּנֹּתָ֔יו מִמֶּ֖נּוּ הָי֣וּ קַרְנֹתָ֑יו וַיְצַ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made its horns on its four corners; from it were its horns; and he overlaid it [with] bronze.

en.L: And he made its horns on its four corners; its horns were from it, and he overlaid it [with] bronze.
en.B: He shaped horns on its four corners, forming part of the altar itself, and overlaid it with bronze.
en.R: He made a horn-shaped point sticking up at each of its four corners. The horns were part of the altar itself, not separate pieces. He covered the altar with bronze.

decisions.choice: its horns were from it: of one piece with the altar
decisions.reason: As in 27:2, the horns were not made separately and fixed on; they were part of the altar's own frame.

decisions.choice: a horn-shaped point sticking up
decisions.reason: Readable describes the horns and spells out "from it", as at 27:2.

source.text: וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֣י הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ אֶת־הַסִּירֹ֤ת וְאֶת־הַיָּעִים֙ וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָקֹ֔ת אֶת־הַמִּזְלָגֹ֖ת וְאֶת־הַמַּחְתֹּ֑ת כָּל־כֵּלָ֖יו עָשָׂ֥ה נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made all the articles of the altar: the pots and the shovels and the basins, the forks and the firepans; all its articles he made [of] bronze.

en.L: And he made all the utensils of the altar: the pots and the shovels and the basins, the forks and the firepans; all its utensils he made [of] bronze.
en.B: He made all the utensils for the altar: the pots, shovels, basins, forks and firepans. He made all its utensils of bronze.
en.R: He made all the tools for the altar out of bronze: the pots, shovels, bowls, forks, and pans for carrying hot coals.

decisions.choice: the altar's tools, as listed in 27:3
decisions.reason: The list matches 27:3: pots for the fatty ashes, shovels, bowls for the blood of the offerings, forks for the meat and pans for burning coals (see the notes there).

decisions.choice: bowls ... pans for carrying hot coals
decisions.reason: As at 27:3, Readable says "bowls" and explains the firepans. Literal and Balanced keep "basins" and "firepans".

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ מִכְבָּ֔ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֶ֣שֶׁת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת תַּ֧חַת כַּרְכֻּבּ֛וֹ מִלְּמַ֖טָּה עַד־חֶצְיֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made for the altar a grating, a work of network [of] bronze, under its ledge, from below up to its middle.

en.L: And he made for the altar a grating, a work of network [of] bronze, under its ledge, from below up to its middle.
en.B: He made for the altar a grating of bronze, worked as a mesh, and set it under its ledge, reaching from below up to the middle of the altar.
en.R: He made a bronze grate shaped like a net for the altar. It was under the ledge that ran around the altar, and it reached halfway up.

decisions.choice: a grating, a work of network: a bronze lattice on the lower half of the altar
decisions.reason: This is the grating of 27:4-5. Whether it was inside the altar or around the outside of its lower half is not said (see the note at 27:4).

decisions.choice: its ledge: a rim or band around the altar, halfway up
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and in 27:5, and its meaning is not certain. It seems to have been a ledge or band around the sides of the altar, with the grating below it.

decisions.choice: set it (Balanced); It was (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the place of the grating straight onto the verb "made". Balanced and Readable add a verb to say where it went.

source.text: וַיִּצֹ֞ק אַרְבַּ֧ע טַבָּעֹ֛ת בְּאַרְבַּ֥ע הַקְּצָוֺ֖ת לְמִכְבַּ֣ר הַנְּחֹ֑שֶׁת בָּתִּ֖ים לַבַּדִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he cast four rings on the four ends of the grating of the bronze, holders for the poles.

en.L: And he cast four rings at the four ends of the bronze grating, holders for the poles.
en.B: He cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, to hold the poles.
en.R: He made four rings out of melted bronze and put them on the four corners of the grate. The rings held the carrying poles.

decisions.choice: cast: made by pouring molten metal into a mold
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour. The rings were cast in molds, as the bases of 26:37 were.

decisions.choice: holders: literally "houses" for the poles
decisions.reason: The rings were places for the poles to pass through, so that the altar could be carried (27:4, 7).

decisions.choice: made out of melted bronze
decisions.reason: Readable explains "cast", as at 26:37.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־הַבַּדִּ֖ים עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made the poles [of] woods of acacia and overlaid them [with] bronze.

en.L: And he made the poles [of] acacia wood and overlaid them [with] bronze.
en.B: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
en.R: He made the carrying poles out of acacia wood and covered them with bronze.

decisions.choice: poles: carrying poles
decisions.reason: As in 27:6, the poles were for carrying the altar when the camp moved (Numbers 4:13-14).

decisions.choice: carrying poles
decisions.reason: Readable says what the poles were for.

source.text: וַיָּבֵ֨א אֶת־הַבַּדִּ֜ים בַּטַּבָּעֹ֗ת עַ֚ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ לָשֵׂ֥את אֹת֖וֹ בָּהֶ֑ם נְב֥וּב לֻחֹ֖ת עָשָׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it by them; hollow [of] boards he made it.

en.L: And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it with them; hollow, [of] boards he made it.
en.B: He slid the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar for carrying it. He built the altar as a hollow box of planks.
en.R: He slid the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, so it could be carried. He made the altar like a hollow box out of boards.

decisions.choice: hollow, of boards: a hollow frame of planks
decisions.reason: As in 27:8, the altar was a box of acacia planks covered with bronze. Whether it was filled with earth or stones where it stood is not said (see the note at 27:8).

source.text: וַיַּ֗עַשׂ אֵ֚ת הַכִּיּ֣וֹר נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וְאֵ֖ת כַּנּ֣וֹ נְחֹ֑שֶׁת בְּמַרְאֹת֙ הַצֹּ֣בְאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר צָֽבְא֔וּ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he made the basin [of] bronze and its stand [of] bronze, with the mirrors of the serving [women] who served [at] the entrance of the tent of meeting.

en.L: And he made the basin [of] bronze and its stand [of] bronze, from the mirrors of the serving women who served [at] the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: He made the basin and its stand of bronze. The bronze came from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.R: He made the basin, a large bronze bowl, and its bronze stand. He made them from the bronze mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

decisions.choice: basin: the large bowl of water for the priests' washing
decisions.reason: This is the basin commanded in 30:18-21, which stood between the tent of meeting and the altar, where the priests washed their hands and feet.

decisions.choice: mirrors: polished metal hand mirrors
decisions.reason: Mirrors in the ancient world were polished discs of bronze or copper. The text does not say how the mirrors came to be used; they may have been among the gifts the women brought (35:22-29).

decisions.choice: the serving women who served: women with some regular service at the entrance of the tent
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb come from the same root, which is used for serving in an army and also for the Levites' work at the tent of meeting (Numbers 4:23; 8:24). The same words are used of women at the entrance of the tent of meeting in 1 Samuel 2:22. What these women did is not said: they may have kept watch, done regular work or gathered to worship there. The tabernacle was not yet set up (40:2, 17), so the tent may be the tent of meeting outside the camp (33:7), or the women may be named by the role they later had. The Greek translation (the Septuagint) reads "the women who fasted".

decisions.choice: a large bronze bowl ... bronze mirrors
decisions.reason: Readable explains "basin", as at 30:18, and says what the mirrors were made of (m2).

source.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת־הֶחָצֵ֑ר לִפְאַ֣ת׀נֶ֣גֶב תֵּימָ֗נָה קַלְעֵ֤י הֶֽחָצֵר֙ שֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֔ר מֵאָ֖ה בָּאַמָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made the courtyard: for the side of the south, southward, the hangings of the courtyard [were of] fine linen twisted, one hundred by the cubit.

en.L: And he made the courtyard. For the south side, southward, the hangings of the courtyard [were of] fine twisted linen, 100 cubits.
en.B: He made the courtyard. On the south side the hangings of the courtyard were of fine twisted linen, {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} long.
en.R: He made the courtyard around the tabernacle. Along the south side he put up hangings made of fine twisted linen, {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} long.

decisions.choice: the courtyard: made as commanded in 27:9-19
decisions.reason: Verses 9-20 follow the instructions of 27:9-19 closely, with a few added details about the silver tops of the pillars (verses 17, 19). The notes on those verses explain the hangings, pillars and bases.

decisions.choice: the south side, southward: the side facing south
decisions.reason: Two words for south stand together, as in 27:9.

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: around the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Readable says where the courtyard was, as at 27:9.

source.text: עַמּוּדֵיהֶ֣ם עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֥ם עֶשְׂרִ֖ים נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וָוֵ֧י הָעַמֻּדִ֛ים וַחֲשֻׁקֵיהֶ֖ם כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: Their pillars twenty and their bases twenty [of] bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver.

en.L: Their pillars [were] twenty and their bases twenty, [of] bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [were of] silver.
en.B: There were twenty pillars in twenty bronze bases, with hooks and bands of silver on the pillars.
en.R: The hangings hung on twenty posts that stood in twenty bronze bases. The posts had silver hooks and silver bands.

decisions.choice: bands: rings around the pillars, or rods between them
decisions.reason: As at 27:10, the word is not certain. It may mean bands around the tops of the pillars or rods running from pillar to pillar (see verse 17).

decisions.choice: posts
decisions.reason: Readable says "posts" for the pillars of the courtyard, as in chapter 27.

source.text: וְלִפְאַ֤ת צָפוֹן֙ מֵאָ֣ה בָֽאַמָּ֔ה עַמּוּדֵיהֶ֣ם עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֥ם עֶשְׂרִ֖ים נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וָוֵ֧י הָֽעַמּוּדִ֛ים וַחֲשֻׁקֵיהֶ֖ם כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And for the side of the north, one hundred by the cubit; their pillars twenty and their bases twenty [of] bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver.

en.L: And for the north side, 100 cubits; their pillars twenty and their bases twenty, [of] bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver.
en.B: The north side was also {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} long, with twenty pillars in twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the pillars.
en.R: The north side was the same: {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} of hangings on twenty posts that stood in twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands.

decisions.choice: the north side: the same as the south side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the length, "one hundred by the cubit"; the hangings are understood from verse 9. The two long sides matched in every detail (27:11).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

source.text: וְלִפְאַת־יָ֗ם קְלָעִים֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה עַמּוּדֵיהֶ֥ם עֲשָׂרָ֔ה וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם עֲשָׂרָ֑ה וָוֵ֧י הָעַמֻּדִ֛ים וַחֲשׁוּקֵיהֶ֖ם כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And for the side of the west, hangings fifty by the cubit; their pillars ten and their bases ten; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver.

en.L: And for the west side, hangings of 50 cubits; their pillars ten and their bases ten; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver.
en.B: On the west side there were hangings {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} long, with ten pillars and ten bases, and silver hooks and bands on the pillars.
en.R: At the west end the hangings were {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} long. They hung on ten posts in ten bases, with silver hooks and bands.

decisions.choice: the west side: literally, the side of the sea
decisions.reason: The Mediterranean Sea lies to the west of the land of Israel, so "sea" is a common word for west (27:12).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

source.text: וְלִפְאַ֛ת קֵ֥דְמָה מִזְרָ֖חָה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַמָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And for the side of the east, toward the sunrise, fifty cubits.

en.L: And for the east side, toward the sunrise, 50 cubits.
en.B: The east side, facing the sunrise, was also {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} wide.
en.R: The east end, facing the sunrise, was also {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: the east side, toward the sunrise: the front of the courtyard
decisions.reason: Two words for east stand together, the second meaning "the place of sunrise", as in 27:13. The gate was on this side (verses 14-18).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

source.text: קְלָעִ֛ים חֲמֵשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה אַמָּ֖ה אֶל־הַכָּתֵ֑ף עַמּוּדֵיהֶ֣ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: Hangings fifteen cubits to the side; their pillars three and their bases three.

en.L: Hangings of 15 cubits to the [one] side; their pillars three and their bases three.
en.B: On one side of the entrance there were hangings {{units:about 22 1/2 feet|15 cubits}} long, with three pillars and three bases.
en.R: On one side of the gate, hangings {{units:about 22 1/2 feet|15 cubits}} long hung on three posts that stood in three bases.

decisions.choice: side: literally "shoulder", the part of the east wall beside the gate
decisions.reason: As in 27:14, the word names the stretch of wall on either side of the gateway.

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: of the entrance / of the gate
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which side is meant, as at 27:14.

source.text: וְלַכָּתֵ֣ף הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית מִזֶּ֤ה וּמִזֶּה֙ לְשַׁ֣עַר הֶֽחָצֵ֔ר קְלָעִ֕ים חֲמֵ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה אַמָּ֑ה עַמֻּדֵיהֶ֣ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And for the second side, from this and from this of the gate of the courtyard, hangings fifteen cubits; their pillars three and their bases three.

en.L: And for the second side, on this [side] and on that [side] of the gate of the courtyard, hangings of 15 cubits; their pillars three and their bases three.
en.B: The other side was the same, so that there were hangings of {{units:about 22 1/2 feet|15 cubits}} on each side of the courtyard gate, with three pillars and three bases.
en.R: The other side of the gate was the same. On each side of the courtyard gate there were hangings {{units:about 22 1/2 feet|15 cubits}} long, each hung on three posts in three bases.

decisions.choice: on this side and on that: on each side of the gate
decisions.reason: The phrase, not found in 27:15, makes clear that both stretches of 15 cubits flanked the gate. With the gate of 20 cubits (verse 18) they make up the 50 cubits of the east end (verse 13).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

source.text: כָּל־קַלְעֵ֧י הֶחָצֵ֛ר סָבִ֖יב שֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: All the hangings of the courtyard all around [were of] fine linen twisted.

en.L: All the hangings of the courtyard all around [were of] fine twisted linen.
en.B: All the hangings around the courtyard were of fine twisted linen.
en.R: All the hangings around the courtyard were made of fine twisted linen.

decisions.choice: fine twisted linen: linen of fine thread spun from several strands
decisions.reason: As in 26:1 and 27:9, the hangings were of fine white linen.

source.text: וְהָאֲדָנִ֣ים לָֽעַמֻּדִים֮ נְחֹשֶׁת֒ וָוֵ֨י הָֽעַמּוּדִ֜ים וַחֲשׁוּקֵיהֶם֙ כֶּ֔סֶף וְצִפּ֥וּי רָאשֵׁיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף וְהֵם֙ מְחֻשָּׁקִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף כֹּ֖ל עַמֻּדֵ֥י הֶחָצֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the bases for the pillars [were of] bronze, the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver, and the overlay of their tops [of] silver; and they [were] banded [with] silver, all the pillars of the courtyard.

en.L: And the bases for the pillars [were of] bronze, the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver, and the overlay of their tops [of] silver; and they [were] banded [with] silver, all the pillars of the courtyard.
en.B: The bases of the pillars were bronze, and the hooks and bands on the pillars were silver. Their tops were overlaid with silver, and every pillar of the courtyard was fitted with silver bands.
en.R: The bases of the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver, and the tops of the posts were covered with silver. Every post around the courtyard had silver bands.

decisions.choice: the overlay of their tops: a silver covering on the top of each pillar
decisions.reason: Chapter 27 does not mention this. The silver for it is counted in verse 28. "Tops" is literally "heads".

decisions.choice: banded with silver: fitted with silver bands
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "bands". Whether the bands ringed each pillar or joined the pillars is not certain (see verse 10; 27:17).

decisions.choice: covered
decisions.reason: Readable says "covered" for "overlaid", as elsewhere in Exodus.

source.text: וּמָסַ֞ךְ שַׁ֤עַר הֶחָצֵר֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה רֹקֵ֔ם תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים אַמָּה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וְקוֹמָ֤ה בְרֹ֨חַב֙ חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת לְעֻמַּ֖ת קַלְעֵ֥י הֶחָצֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the screen of the gate of the courtyard [was the] work of an embroiderer, [of] blue and purple and scarlet and fine linen twisted; and twenty cubits [the] length, and the height in breadth five cubits, corresponding to the hangings of the courtyard.

en.L: And the screen of the gate of the courtyard [was] the work of an embroiderer, [of] blue and purple and scarlet [yarn] and fine twisted linen; and 20 cubits [was the] length, and the height, in breadth, 5 cubits, corresponding to the hangings of the courtyard.
en.B: The screen for the courtyard gate was worked in colors by an embroiderer, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. It was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} long and {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} high, matching the hangings of the courtyard.
en.R: The screen for the gate of the courtyard was made by a skilled worker in colorful patterns, using blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. It was {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide and {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} high, the same height as the courtyard hangings.

decisions.choice: the height, in breadth: the height of the cloth, from top to bottom
decisions.reason: The width of the woven cloth was the height of the screen as it hung. It was 5 cubits, the same as the hangings (27:18).

decisions.choice: the work of an embroiderer: work in colored thread
decisions.reason: As at 27:16, whether the designs were sewn with a needle or woven into the cloth is not certain.

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: wide
decisions.reason: The length of the screen ran across the gateway, so Readable calls it the width. Literal and Balanced keep "length".

source.text: וְעַמֻּֽדֵיהֶם֙ אַרְבָּעָ֔ה וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֥ם אַרְבָּעָ֖ה נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וָוֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף וְצִפּ֧וּי רָאשֵׁיהֶ֛ם וַחֲשֻׁקֵיהֶ֖ם כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And their pillars four and their bases four [of] bronze, their hooks [of] silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands [of] silver.

en.L: And their pillars [were] four and their bases four, [of] bronze; their hooks [were of] silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands [of] silver.
en.B: It hung on four pillars set in four bronze bases. Their hooks were silver, and so were the overlay on their tops and their bands.
en.R: It hung on four posts that stood in four bronze bases. The posts had silver hooks and silver bands, and their tops were covered with silver.

decisions.choice: their pillars: the pillars of the gate's screen
decisions.reason: "Their" refers to the screen of verse 18, which hung on four pillars (27:16).

decisions.choice: It hung on
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the pillars relate to the screen of verse 18.

source.text: וְֽכָל־הַיְתֵדֹ֞ת לַמִּשְׁכָּ֧ן וְלֶחָצֵ֛ר סָבִ֖יב נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And all the pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard all around [were of] bronze.

en.L: And all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard all around [were of] bronze.
en.B: All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard around it were bronze.
en.R: All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard around it were made of bronze.

decisions.choice: tent pegs: pegs driven into the ground to hold the cords
decisions.reason: As in 27:19, the pegs held down the cords of the tabernacle and of the courtyard hangings.

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה פְקוּדֵ֤י הַמִּשְׁכָּן֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר פֻּקַּ֖ד עַל־פִּ֣י מֹשֶׁ֑ה עֲבֹדַת֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם בְּיַד֙ אִֽיתָמָ֔ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are] the counted things of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, which were counted by the mouth of Moses, the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

en.L: These [are] the records of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, which were counted by the mouth of Moses, [as] the work of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
en.B: This is the record of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, as it was counted at Moses' command. The counting was the work of the Levites, led by Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
en.R: Here is a list of the materials used for the tabernacle, the tent where the covenant tablets were kept. Moses ordered the Levites to count them, and Ithamar son of Aaron the priest was in charge of the work.

decisions.choice: the records ... counted: a tally of what was used
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root used for counting and enrolling people (verses 25-26; 30:12-14). Here it means the reckoning of the metals that went into the tabernacle (verses 24-31).

decisions.choice: the tabernacle of the testimony: the tent that held the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: The testimony is the tablets of the covenant kept in the ark (25:16, 21). The same name for the tabernacle is used in Numbers 1:50, 53.

decisions.choice: the work of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar: the Levites did the counting under Ithamar
decisions.reason: Ithamar was Aaron's youngest son (6:23; 28:1). In Numbers he oversees the Levite clans of Gershon and Merari, who carried the tabernacle (Numbers 4:28, 33). The phrase "the work of the Levites" stands loosely in the sentence; it most likely means that the counting was done by the Levites under Ithamar.

decisions.choice: The counting was the work of the Levites (Balanced); Moses ordered the Levites to count them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make "the work of the Levites" a sentence of its own (m3).

decisions.choice: a list of the materials ... where the covenant tablets were kept
decisions.reason: Readable says what was counted (verses 24-31) and explains "the testimony".

source.text: וּבְצַלְאֵ֛ל בֶּן־אוּרִ֥י בֶן־ח֖וּר לְמַטֵּ֣ה יְהוּדָ֑ה עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that commanded Yahweh Moses.

en.L: And Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.
en.B: It was Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, who made all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.
en.R: Bezalel son of Uri and grandson of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, made everything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: Bezalel: the craftsman God chose to lead the work
decisions.reason: God called Bezalel by name and filled him with the Spirit of God for the work (31:2-5; 35:30-35). His family line is given in 1 Chronicles 2:18-20.

decisions.choice: all that the LORD had commanded Moses: the work matched God's command
decisions.reason: The phrase sums up the building. It becomes a refrain in chapters 39-40, where each part is made "as the LORD had commanded Moses" (39:1, 5, 43; 40:16, 19).

decisions.choice: grandson
decisions.reason: Readable calls Bezalel the grandson of Hur, as at 31:2.

source.text: וְאִתּ֗וֹ אָהֳלִיאָ֞ב בֶּן־אֲחִיסָמָ֛ךְ לְמַטֵּה־דָ֖ן חָרָ֣שׁ וְחֹשֵׁ֑ב וְרֹקֵ֗ם בַּתְּכֵ֨לֶת֙ וּבָֽאַרְגָּמָ֔ן וּבְתוֹלַ֥עַת הַשָּׁנִ֖י וּבַשֵּֽׁשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and a designer and an embroiderer in blue and in purple and in scarlet and in fine linen.

en.L: And with him [was] Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and a designer and an embroiderer in blue and in purple and in scarlet [yarn] and in fine linen.
en.B: With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and designer, who also worked in colors with blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
en.R: Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, worked with him. Oholiab could engrave and create designs. He also made colorful patterns in cloth with blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen.

decisions.choice: Oholiab: Bezalel's partner from the tribe of Dan
decisions.reason: God appointed Oholiab to work with Bezalel (31:6) and gave both of them the ability to teach others (35:34).

decisions.choice: engraver, designer, embroiderer: three kinds of skilled work
decisions.reason: The first word means a craftsman who cuts or engraves in stone, wood or metal (28:11). The second is the skilled designer whose work is in 26:1. The third is the worker in colored thread of 26:36 and 27:16.

decisions.choice: made colorful patterns in cloth
decisions.reason: Readable describes the embroiderer's work without deciding between needlework and weaving, as at 27:16.

source.text: כָּל־הַזָּהָ֗ב הֶֽעָשׂוּי֙ לַמְּלָאכָ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וַיְהִ֣י׀זְהַ֣ב הַתְּנוּפָ֗ה תֵּ֤שַׁע וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ כִּכָּ֔ר וּשְׁבַ֨ע מֵא֧וֹת וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: All the gold that was used for the work in all the work of the holy place, and it was the gold of the wave offering, [was] twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels by the shekel of the holy place.

en.L: All the gold that was used for the work, in all the work of the sanctuary, and it was the gold of the wave offering, [was] 29 talents and 730 shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
en.B: All the gold used for the work, for all the work on the sanctuary, was gold given as an offering. It came to {{units:about 2,200 pounds|29 talents and 730 shekels}}, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
en.R: All the gold the people gave for the work on the sanctuary came to {{units:about 2,200 pounds|29 talents and 730 shekels}}, weighed by the official sanctuary shekel.

decisions.choice: the wave offering: a gift presented before the LORD
decisions.reason: The word names an offering lifted or waved before the LORD to give it to him. Here it is the gold the people brought in 35:22.

decisions.choice: 29 talents and 730 shekels: about 2,200 pounds (about 1,000 kilograms) of gold
decisions.reason: A shekel weighed about two-fifths of an ounce (11.5 grams), and a talent was 3,000 shekels, about 75 pounds (verses 25-26 show this). So 29 x 3,000 + 730 = 87,730 shekels; 87,730 x 2/5 ounce = about 35,100 ounces, which is about 2,190 pounds. The figures are approximate: ancient weights varied, and the shekel's weight is known only roughly. On the same reckoning the silver (verse 25) is about 7,500 pounds and the bronze (verse 29) about 5,300 pounds.

decisions.choice: the shekel of the sanctuary: the standard weight used for payments to God
decisions.reason: As in 30:13, the sanctuary shekel was the standard of twenty gerahs (Leviticus 27:25).

decisions.choice: modern weight first, talents and shekels as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds by default, rounded and marked "about", with the talents and shekels of the Hebrew as the units alternative (see the notes at verse 24). Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: the people gave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the gold the people gave" for "the gold of the wave offering" (m1). Literal keeps "wave offering"; Balanced says "given as an offering".

source.text: וְכֶ֛סֶף פְּקוּדֵ֥י הָעֵדָ֖ה מְאַ֣ת כִּכָּ֑ר וְאֶלֶף֩ וּשְׁבַ֨ע מֵא֜וֹת וַחֲמִשָּׁ֧ה וְשִׁבְעִ֛ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the silver of the enrolled of the congregation [was] one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels by the shekel of the holy place.

en.L: And the silver of those enrolled of the congregation [was] 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
en.B: The silver given by those of the community who were enrolled weighed {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents and 1,775 shekels}}, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
en.R: The silver from the men of the community who were counted came to {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents and 1,775 shekels}}, weighed by the official sanctuary shekel.

decisions.choice: the silver of those enrolled: the half-shekel ransom of 30:11-16
decisions.reason: Each man counted paid half a shekel as a ransom for his life, and the silver was given for the service of the tent of meeting (30:12-16). Verse 26 gives the reckoning.

decisions.choice: 100 talents and 1,775 shekels: about 7,500 pounds (about 3,500 kilograms) of silver
decisions.reason: 100 x 3,000 + 1,775 = 301,775 shekels; 301,775 x 2/5 ounce = about 120,700 ounces, which is about 7,540 pounds. The figure is approximate (see the note at verse 24).

decisions.choice: modern weight first, talents and shekels as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds by default, rounded and marked "about", with the talents and shekels of the Hebrew as the units alternative (see the notes at verse 24). Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: community
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "community" for the congregation of Israel; Literal keeps "congregation".

source.text: בֶּ֚קַע לַגֻּלְגֹּ֔לֶת מַחֲצִ֥ית הַשֶּׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ לְכֹ֨ל הָעֹבֵ֜ר עַל־הַפְּקֻדִ֗ים מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה לְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֨לֶף֙ וּשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֔ים וַחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת וַחֲמִשִּֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: A beka for a head, half of the shekel by the shekel of the holy place, for everyone who passed over to the enrolled, from a son of twenty years and upward, for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty.

en.L: A beka per head, half of the shekel by the shekel of the sanctuary, for everyone who passed over to those enrolled, from a son of twenty years and upward, for 603,550 [men].
en.B: That was {{units:about 1/5 ounce|a beka}} a head, half a shekel by the shekel of the sanctuary, from every man twenty years old and up who crossed over to join those enrolled, 603,550 men in all.
en.R: Each man twenty years old or older who was counted gave {{units:about 1/5 ounce|a beka}} of silver, which is half a shekel by the official sanctuary shekel. There were 603,550 men.

decisions.choice: a beka: half a shekel, about a fifth of an ounce (about 5.7 grams)
decisions.reason: The verse itself defines the beka as half a shekel. The same weight is used for the gold nose ring of Genesis 24:22.

decisions.choice: the arithmetic: 603,550 half shekels make 100 talents and 1,775 shekels
decisions.reason: 603,550 x 1/2 = 301,775 shekels. That is the 100 talents and 1,775 shekels of verse 25 if a talent is 3,000 shekels (100 x 3,000 = 300,000, plus 1,775). These verses are how the weight of the talent is known.

decisions.choice: 603,550: the number of the men counted
decisions.reason: The men twenty years and older are counted as in 30:14. The total is the same as the census in Numbers 1:46 and 2:32. Compare "about 600,000 men on foot" in 12:37.

decisions.choice: modern weight first, the beka as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds by default, rounded and marked "about", with the talents and shekels of the Hebrew as the units alternative (see the notes at verse 24). Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: man / men
decisions.reason: The men counted were those twenty years and older (30:14; Numbers 1:3), so Balanced and Readable say "man" and need no gender span.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י מְאַת֙ כִּכַּ֣ר הַכֶּ֔סֶף לָצֶ֗קֶת אֵ֚ת אַדְנֵ֣י הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וְאֵ֖ת אַדְנֵ֣י הַפָּרֹ֑כֶת מְאַ֧ת אֲדָנִ֛ים לִמְאַ֥ת הַכִּכָּ֖ר כִּכָּ֥ר לָאָֽדֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And the one hundred talents of the silver were for casting the bases of the holy place and the bases of the veil; one hundred bases for the one hundred talents, a talent for a base.

en.L: And the 100 talents of silver were for casting the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil: 100 bases for the 100 talents, a talent per base.
en.B: The {{units:7,500 pounds or so|100 talents}} of silver went to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the curtain. There were 100 bases, and each took {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}}.
en.R: The silver, {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents}}, was melted and poured into molds to make the bases for the sanctuary and for the curtain. There were 100 bases, so each base used {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of silver.

decisions.choice: 100 bases, a talent each: 96 for the frames and 4 for the veil
decisions.reason: The frames of the tabernacle stood on 96 silver bases: 40 on the south side, 40 on the north and 16 at the back (26:19-25). The four pillars of the veil stood on 4 more (26:32). 96 + 4 = 100. A talent of silver for each base is about 75 pounds.

decisions.choice: the veil: the inner curtain before the most holy place
decisions.reason: This is the veil of 26:31-33, which divided the holy place from the most holy place.

decisions.choice: modern weight first, talents and shekels as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds by default, rounded and marked "about", with the talents and shekels of the Hebrew as the units alternative (see the notes at verse 24). Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: curtain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "curtain" for the inner veil, as in 26:31-35. Literal keeps "veil".

decisions.choice: melted and poured into molds
decisions.reason: Readable explains "casting", as at 26:37.

source.text: וְאֶת־הָאֶ֜לֶף וּשְׁבַ֤ע הַמֵּאוֹת֙ וַחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה וְשִׁבְעִ֔ים עָשָׂ֥ה וָוִ֖ים לָעַמּוּדִ֑ים וְצִפָּ֥ה רָאשֵׁיהֶ֖ם וְחִשַּׁ֥ק אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five he made hooks for the pillars, and he overlaid their tops and banded them.

en.L: And [of] the 1,775 [shekels] he made hooks for the pillars, and he overlaid their tops and banded them.
en.B: From the remaining {{units:45 pounds or so|1,775 shekels}} he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their tops and fitted them with bands.
en.R: He used the other {{units:45 pounds or so|1,775 shekels}} of silver to make hooks for the posts, to cover their tops, and to make bands for them.

decisions.choice: the 1,775: the shekels left over after the 100 talents
decisions.reason: The unit is not repeated; it is the 1,775 shekels of verse 25. 1,775 x 2/5 ounce = 710 ounces, about 44 pounds (about 20 kilograms). The figure is approximate.

decisions.choice: the pillars: the pillars of the courtyard
decisions.reason: The pillars with silver hooks, tops and bands are those of the courtyard and its gate (verses 10-19). The pillars inside had gold hooks (26:32, 37).

decisions.choice: modern weight first, talents and shekels as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds by default, rounded and marked "about", with the talents and shekels of the Hebrew as the units alternative (see the notes at verse 24). Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: remaining / other
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that these shekels are the rest of the silver of verse 25.

source.text: וּנְחֹ֥שֶׁת הַתְּנוּפָ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֣ים כִּכָּ֑ר וְאַלְפַּ֥יִם וְאַרְבַּע־מֵא֖וֹת שָֽׁקֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: And the bronze of the wave offering [was] seventy talents and two thousand and four hundred shekels.

en.L: And the bronze of the wave offering [was] 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.
en.B: The bronze given as an offering came to {{units:about 5,300 pounds|70 talents and 2,400 shekels}}.
en.R: The bronze the people gave weighed {{units:about 5,300 pounds|70 talents and 2,400 shekels}}.

decisions.choice: 70 talents and 2,400 shekels: about 5,300 pounds (about 2,400 kilograms) of bronze
decisions.reason: 70 x 3,000 + 2,400 = 212,400 shekels; 212,400 x 2/5 ounce = about 85,000 ounces, which is about 5,310 pounds. The figure is approximate (see the note at verse 24).

decisions.choice: the wave offering: the bronze the people presented
decisions.reason: As in verse 24, the bronze was a gift presented before the LORD (35:24).

decisions.choice: modern weight first, talents and shekels as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds by default, rounded and marked "about", with the talents and shekels of the Hebrew as the units alternative (see the notes at verse 24). Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: the people gave
decisions.reason: Readable says who gave the offering, as in verse 24.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בָּ֗הּ אֶת־אַדְנֵי֙ פֶּ֚תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְאֵת֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַנְּחֹ֔שֶׁת וְאֶת־מִכְבַּ֥ר הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made with it the bases of the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the altar of the bronze, and the grating of the bronze which [was] for it, and all the articles of the altar,

en.L: And with it he made the bases of the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the bronze altar, and the bronze grating that [was] for it, and all the utensils of the altar,
en.B: Out of it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar together with the bronze grating that belonged to it, all the utensils of the altar,
en.R: He used this bronze to make the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grate, and all the tools for the altar.

decisions.choice: the bases of the entrance: the five bronze bases of the entrance screen
decisions.reason: The screen at the entrance of the tent hung on five pillars set in five bronze bases (26:37).

decisions.choice: with it: with the bronze of verse 29
decisions.reason: The list of what was made from the bronze runs on into verse 31.

source.text: וְאֶת־אַדְנֵ֤י הֶֽחָצֵר֙ סָבִ֔יב וְאֶת־אַדְנֵ֖י שַׁ֣עַר הֶחָצֵ֑ר וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־יִתְדֹ֧ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן וְאֶת־כָּל־יִתְדֹ֥ת הֶחָצֵ֖ר סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: and the bases of the courtyard all around, and the bases of the gate of the courtyard, and all the pegs of the tabernacle, and all the pegs of the courtyard all around.

en.L: and the bases of the courtyard all around, and the bases of the gate of the courtyard, and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle, and all the tent pegs of the courtyard all around.
en.B: the bases all around the courtyard, the bases of the courtyard gate, and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the courtyard on every side.
en.R: He also used it to make the bases for the posts around the courtyard and at its gate, and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard.

decisions.choice: the bases of the courtyard and of its gate: sixty bronze bases
decisions.reason: The courtyard's pillars stood on 20 + 20 + 10 + 3 + 3 bronze bases, and the gate's on 4 more (verses 10-19), sixty in all.

decisions.choice: tent pegs: the bronze pegs of verse 20
decisions.reason: The pegs held the cords of the tabernacle and of the courtyard hangings (27:19).

decisions.choice: He also used it to make ... for the posts
decisions.reason: Readable ends verse 30 with a full stop and repeats the verb here, and says that the bases held the posts.
